items.title: 脆弱的力量
items.author: Brené Brown · TED
items.en: Brené Brown spent years studying vulnerability, and what she found overturned her own assumptions. We live in a culture that tells us vulnerability is weakness, yet the data points the other way: vulnerability is actually the birthplace of love, belonging, joy, and creativity. The people who feel most connected are the ones willing to be seen, imperfections and all. Numbing the hard emotions does not selectively work—when we numb fear and shame, we also numb joy and gratitude. The courage to be imperfect, to say 'I love you' first, to do something where there are no guarantees—that is where wholehearted living begins.
items.zh: 布琳·布朗花数年研究“脆弱”，结果推翻了她自己的假设。我们身处的文化告诉我们脆弱是软弱，但数据指向相反的方向：脆弱其实是爱、归属、喜悦与创造力的诞生地。那些感到最联结的人，正是愿意被看见的人，连同所有不完美。麻痹难受的情绪并不会“选择性生效”——当我们麻痹恐惧与羞耻，也一并麻痹了喜悦与感恩。敢于不完美、敢先说“我爱你”、敢做没有保证的事——全心全意的生活正由此开始。
items.note: vulnerability 脆弱；assumption 假设；birthplace 诞生地；numb 麻痹；wholehearted 全心全意的。

items.title: 从“为什么”开始
items.author: Simon Sinek · TED
items.en: Simon Sinek noticed that great leaders and companies all communicate in the opposite direction from everyone else. Most people start with what they do, then how, and rarely reach why. But inspiring leaders begin with why—a purpose, a cause, a belief. The 'Golden Circle' explains why some organizations move people while others do not. It is not about facts and features; people do not buy what you make, they buy why you make it. When you start with why, you attract those who believe what you believe—and that shared belief is what turns customers into loyal followers.
items.zh: 西蒙·斯涅克发现，伟大的领导者与公司，沟通方向与常人相反。多数人从“做什么”开始，再到“怎么做”，却很少触及“为什么”。而鼓舞人心的领导者从“为什么”开始——一个目的、一个缘由、一份信念。“黄金圈”解释了为何有些组织能打动人，有些却不能。关键不在事实与功能：人们买的不是你做什么，而是你为什么做。当你从“为什么”出发，便吸引来那些与你信念相同的人——正是这份共同信念，把顾客变成忠实的追随者。
items.note: communicate 沟通；inspiring 鼓舞人心的；feature 功能；loyal 忠实的；attract 吸引。

items.title: 拖延症患者的大脑
items.author: Tim Urban · TED
items.en: Tim Urban realized that the brain of a chronic procrastinator contains an Instant Gratification Monkey that hijacks the steering wheel, abandoning long-term goals for easy, fun tasks. The Rational Decision-Maker is left helpless—until the Panic Monster appears. The Panic Monster is the only thing the monkey fears, and it awakens whenever a deadline looms or public embarrassment threatens. The problem with long-term projects is that the monster never shows up, so we surf the internet while quietly ruining our future selves. The antidote is simple: notice the monkey, and shrink every big task into the smallest possible first step.
items.zh: 蒂姆·厄本发现，拖延症患者的大脑里住着一只“即时满足猴”，它会抢走方向盘，为了轻松有趣的事抛下长期目标，留下“理性决策者”无能为力——直到“恐慌怪兽”出现。恐慌怪兽是猴子唯一害怕的东西，它在截止日逼近或当众出丑的威胁降临时苏醒。长期项目的问题在于怪兽从不出现，于是我们一边上网冲浪，一边悄悄毁掉未来的自己。解药很简单：察觉那只猴子，并把每个大任务拆成尽可能小的第一步。
items.note: chronic 长期的；gratification 满足；hijack 劫持；deadline 截止日；antidote 解药。

items.title: 坚毅：激情与毅力
items.author: Angela Duckworth · TED
items.en: Angela Duckworth left a high-flying consulting job to teach seventh graders math, and she noticed something puzzling: the most successful students were not always the most talented. Some naturally gifted kids struggled, while others with average ability pushed through. After years of research across cadets, salespeople, and students, one trait predicted success more than IQ or talent: grit. Grit is passion and perseverance for long-term goals—the stamina to keep going after failure, to treat life as a marathon rather than a sprint. Talent is how quickly you improve with effort, but effort counts twice: it builds skill, and then turns skill into achievement.
items.zh: 安杰拉·达克沃斯离开光鲜的咨询工作去教初一数学，她发现一件令人困惑的事：最成功的学生未必最有天赋。一些天赋出众的孩子苦苦挣扎，而能力平平者却坚持下来。经过多年对学员、销售与学生的研究，有一个特质比智商或天赋更能预测成功：坚毅。坚毅是对长期目标的激情与毅力——在失败后继续前行的耐力，把人生当作马拉松而非短跑。天赋决定你努力时进步的快慢，但努力要算两次：它构建技能，再把技能转化为成就。
items.note: puzzling 令人困惑的；gifted 有天赋的；perseverance 毅力；stamina 耐力；achievement 成就。

items.title: 身体语言塑造你自己
items.author: Amy Cuddy · TED
items.en: Amy Cuddy's research asks a simple question: does our body language affect how others see us, and also how we see ourselves? Power poses—expanding the body, taking up space—have measurable effects: after just two minutes, they lower stress hormones and raise confidence markers. The finding is not about faking strength to impress others, but about genuinely changing your own physiology. Her advice is the two-minute rule: before a stressful situation, stand like Wonder Woman in private. You may not yet feel confident, but tiny postural changes can nudge your mind to catch up. 'Fake it till you become it.'
items.zh: 艾米·卡迪的研究提出了一个简单的问题：身体语言是否影响别人对我们的看法，也影响我们对自己的看法？力量姿势——舒展身体、占据空间——有可测量的效果：仅两分钟后，压力激素下降，自信指标上升。这个发现并非教你假装强大去取悦他人，而是真正改变自身的生理状态。她的建议是“两分钟法则”：在压力情境前，私下像神奇女侠那样站立。你也许还没感到自信，但微小的姿态改变能推动心智跟上。“假装，直到你成为它。”
items.note: measurable 可测量的；hormone 激素；physiology 生理；postural 姿态的；nudge 推动。

items.title: 成长型思维的力量
items.author: Carol Dweck · TED
items.en: Carol Dweck identified two mindsets that shape how people approach challenge. In a fixed mindset, people believe ability is set—you either have it or you don't, so failure means 'I'm not good enough.' In a growth mindset, people believe abilities can be developed through effort and strategy, so failure becomes information about what to try next. The word that signals growth is 'yet': not 'I can't do this,' but 'I can't do this yet.' Praising intelligence can actually shrink children's willingness to take risks, while praising effort and process builds resilience. When we reframe difficulty as the workout that grows the brain, learning stops being a verdict and becomes a path.
items.zh: 卡罗尔·德韦克发现了两种影响人们面对挑战的思维模式。固定型思维的人相信能力是天定的——你有就是有，没有就是没有，于是失败意味着“我不够好”。成长型思维的人相信能力可以通过努力和策略发展，于是失败变成了“下一步该试什么”的信息。标志着成长的词是“还”：不是“我做不到”，而是“我还做不到”。夸赞聪明反而会减少孩子冒险的意愿，而夸赞努力与过程则建立韧性。当我们把困难重新框定为锻炼大脑的“训练”，学习就不再是判决，而成为一条路径。
items.note: mindset 思维模式；fixed 固定的；strategy 策略；resilience 韧性；verdict 判决。

items.title: 快乐的优势
items.author: Shawn Achor · TED
items.en: Shawn Achor argues that we have the formula backwards. We think success leads to happiness, but the brain actually works the other way: a positive brain performs better on nearly every measure—creativity, energy, productivity. If happiness is the goal, we should raise optimism in the present, not chase it after the next achievement. His research found that small daily habits rewire the brain over three weeks: write down three gratitudes, journal one positive experience, exercise, meditate, and send a kind email. Happiness, it turns out, is not the finish line of success; it is the starting line of performance.
items.zh: 肖恩·阿克尔认为我们把公式弄反了。我们以为成功会带来快乐，但大脑其实反过来运作：积极的大脑在几乎每一项指标上都表现更好——创造力、精力、生产力。如果快乐是目标，我们应该在当下提升乐观，而非等到下一个成就之后。他的研究发现，一些小小的日常习惯能在三周内重塑大脑：写下三件感恩、记录一段正向经历、运动、冥想、发一封善意的邮件。原来快乐并非成功的终点线，而是表现的起跑线。
items.note: formula 公式；optimism 乐观；achievement 成就；journal 记日记；meditate 冥想。

items.title: 尝试新事物30天
items.author: Matt Cutts · TED
items.en: Matt Cutts offers a tiny, practical idea: try something new for 30 days. The logic is that 30 days is just long enough to form a habit and just short enough to feel approachable. Instead of vague year-long resolutions that quietly fade by February, pick one concrete challenge: take a photo every day, write 1,500 words, bike to work, give up sugar. Two things tend to happen. First, the days become more memorable, because each one contains a small new thread. Second, self-confidence grows as you prove, month after month, that you can keep a promise to yourself. Small changes, sustained, are anything but small.
items.zh: 马特·卡茨提出了一个小而实用的点子：用30天尝试一件新事。逻辑是，30天既够长以养成习惯，又够短以让人觉得可亲近。与其立下模糊的年度决心、到二月便悄悄消散，不如挑一个具体的挑战：每天拍一张照、写1500字、骑车上班、戒糖。往往有两件事会发生：其一，日子变得更难忘，因为每一天都多了一条小小的新的线索；其二，自信心会增长，因为你一个月接一个月地向自己证明：你能对自己信守承诺。微小的改变，若能持续，就一点都不小。
items.note: approachable 可亲近的；vague 模糊的；resolution 决心；concrete 具体的；sustain 持续。

items.title: 内向者的力量
items.author: Susan Cain · TED
items.en: Susan Cain argues that we live in a culture that idolizes extroversion, yet some of the most thoughtful leaders and artists draw their strength from solitude. Introverts prefer to work independently, listen more than they speak, and dive deeply into a single subject rather than skimming the surface of many. The world needs both the orchid and the dandelion. When we force quiet minds to pretend to be loud, we lose the slow, careful thinking that solves hard problems. The task is not to remake introverts, but to let them contribute in the way they do best.
items.zh: 苏珊·凯恩认为，我们身处一个崇拜外向的文化，然而一些最有思想的领导者和艺术家，力量恰恰来自独处。内向者偏爱独立工作、多听少说，并深深潜入单一主题，而非在许多事物表面浅尝辄止。世界既需要兰花，也需要蒲公英。当我们强迫安静的头脑假装喧闹，便失去了那种缓慢而审慎、能解决难题的思考。任务不是改造内向者，而是让他们以最擅长的方式贡献。
items.note: idolize 崇拜；solitude 独处；introvert 内向者；skimming 浅尝；remake 改造。

items.title: 压力是你的朋友
items.author: Kelly McGonigal · TED
items.en: Kelly McGonigal reframes stress as the body's way of preparing us to meet a challenge. When we view our pounding heart as helpful, energy to rise to the occasion, the physical response becomes less harmful. A landmark study found that people who experienced high stress but cared for others had the lowest risk of death, suggesting it is not stress itself but the belief that it is harmful that hurts us. The most stressed yet healthiest individuals were those who spent time helping others. So the next time you feel overwhelmed, tell yourself: my body is gearing up to help me. Then reach out to someone else.
items.zh: 凯莉·麦戈尼格尔把压力重新框定为身体为我们迎接挑战所做的准备。当我们把怦然心跳看作助力，是起身应战的energy，生理反应便不再那么有害。一项标志性研究发现，经历高压却关爱他人的人，死亡风险最低，这说明伤害我们的并非压力本身，而是压力有害这个信念。压力最大却最健康的人，恰恰是那些花时间帮助他人的人。所以下次你感到不堪重负，告诉自己：我的身体正在为我动员能量。然后去靠近另一个人。
items.note: reframe 重新框定；pounding 怦怦跳的；landmark 标志性的；overwhelmed 不堪重负的；gear 动员。

items.title: 失败的价值
items.author: Anonymous · TED
items.en: Too many of us treat failure as a verdict rather than data. In truth, every setback carries a quiet instruction: what to adjust, what to abandon, what to try next. Inventors rarely succeed on the first attempt; they succeed on the last one, after a long chain of small, informative failures. The fear of looking foolish keeps us inside a narrow comfort zone, while the willingness to be wrong expands it. If you are not failing sometimes, you are probably not attempting anything worth failing at. Failure is not the opposite of success; it is part of the route.
items.zh: 我们太多人把失败当成定论，而非数据。其实，每一次挫败都藏着一句安静的指引：该调整什么、舍弃什么、下一步试什么。发明家极少一次成功；他们是在一长串微小而有益的失败之后，才迎来最后一次成功。怕显得愚蠢让我们困在狭窄的舒适区，而敢于犯错则拓展它。如果你从没失败过，大概也没在尝试什么值得失败的事。失败不是成功的对立面，而是通往它的路的一部分。
items.note: verdict 定论；setback 挫折；informative 有益的；foolish 愚蠢的；opposite 对立面。

items.title: 重拾专注
items.author: Anonymous · TED
items.en: Our attention is the most valuable currency we have, yet it is constantly auctioned off to the highest bidder, every notification, every feed, every glowing rectangle. To reclaim focus is not to reject technology, but to decide in advance what deserves our mind. Attention resets in boredom; the empty minute is not wasted but fertile. When we protect a single task from interruption, we give it the depth that makes work meaningful. Concentration is a muscle: it weakens when unused and grows when exercised, one quiet hour at a time.
items.zh: 我们的注意力是所拥有的最值钱的货币，却不断被拍卖给出价最高的人，每条通知、每条信息流、每块发光的屏幕。重拾专注不是拒绝科技，而是提前决定什么配得上我们的心智。注意力在无聊中重置；空白的一分钟不是被浪费，而是肥沃的。当我们保护一项任务不被打断，便赋予它让工作有意义所需的深度。专注是一块肌肉：不用则弱，练则强，一次安静的一小时。
items.note: currency 货币；auction 拍卖；reclaim 重拾；fertile 肥沃的；concentration 专注。
